programmes.name: National Access Summer School (NASS)
programmes.summary: A free four-day, three-night residential at Birmingham for Year 12 students from under-represented backgrounds, with taster lectures, life in halls and e-mentoring afterwards.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students at state schools in England and Wales whose school is a Pathways to Birmingham partner and who meet the Pathways to Birmingham criteria. Students at a Pathways to Birmingham partner school or college (state-funded, non-selective through GCSEs) with Home fee status, who have been in care OR meet at least three measures: free school meals in the last 6 years; school below national average; low-progression postcode (TUNDRA/POLAR quintile 1 or IMD decile 1-2 count as two points; quintile 2 or IMD decile 3-4 one point); first generation; household income below £42,875; disability or long-term illness; estranged; young carer. Meeting two plus significant extenuating circumstances can also be considered.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Students at a Pathways to Birmingham partner school or college (state-funded, non-selective through GCSEs) with Home fee status, who have been in care OR meet at least three measures: free school meals in the last 6 years; school below national average; low-progression postcode (TUNDRA/POLAR quintile 1 or IMD decile 1-2 count as two points; quintile 2 or IMD decile 3-4 one point); first generation; household income below £42,875; disability or long-term illness; estranged; young carer. Meeting two plus significant extenuating circumstances can also be considered. If your school isn't a partner but you think you're eligible, the page says to email the NASS team.
benefits: Pathways to Birmingham offer at Birmingham, typically up to two A-level grades lower (e.g. BBB rather than AAB), if Birmingham is your firm choice
Eligible for Pathways to Birmingham financial support
Guaranteed interviews for Medicine, Dentistry, Nursing, Physiotherapy and Pharmacy

notes: No admissions test (TMUA or other) is listed for any of these courses.

Birmingham's alternative offers (EPQ, Core Maths, music, sport, contextual, Pathways) apply only if Birmingham is your firm choice, and only one reduction is applied: 'we will only apply one reduction to your offer (i.e. these are not stackable, except for EDCAP)'.
From 2027 entry the EPQ and Core Maths alternative offers need grade B (previously grade A); reductions are not applied to a subject the offer specifically requires.
Around 10% of Birmingham's annual undergraduate intake has come through a Pathways to Birmingham programme in recent years (Birmingham widening participation page).
Pathways to Birmingham programmes need the student's school or college to be a P2B partner and a nominated teacher to support the application.
Birmingham names Realising Opportunities in its A2B rules (you can't do A2B if you've already completed RO) but doesn't publish a separate RO alternative offer on the pages checked.
